    "For Success (binary: 0/1), use logistic regression or chi-squared test of independence rather than standard ANOVA, as the mean=0.73 with binary distribution violates normality assumptions",
    "Include Mouse as a blocking factor or random effect in all models to account for 8 mice contributing repeated measures (n=76655 total observations, unequal per mouse: 7233-10986)",
    "Use Type III sums of squares to handle unbalanced design (Combined n=48846 vs Sham n=3505)",
    "Report eta-squared or partial eta-squared as effect size measures"
  ],

    "For continuous variables showing significant ANOVA effects, conduct pairwise comparisons between all 10 pairs of stimulation paradigms",
    "Use Tukey's HSD for balanced comparisons where possible, or Tukey-Kramer for unequal sample sizes",
    "For Success (binary outcome), use pairwise logistic regression with Bonferroni correction or emmeans with logit link",
    "Focus comparisons on Sham vs active conditions and Combined vs unimodal conditions given theoretical interest",
    "Report 95% confidence intervals for all pairwise differences"
  ],
  "multiple_comparison_strategy": "Bonferroni correction for 10 pairwise comparisons per response variable (family-wise alpha = 0.05/10 = 0.005 per test); alternatively, use Holm-Bonferroni for improved power while maintaining strong control of family-wise error rate; for the 5 response variables, consider separate families or overall Bonferroni with alpha = 0.01",
  "predictive_model_recommendation": "Multinomial logistic regression is explicitly recommended as the primary predictive model because Stim Paradigm is categorical with 5 unordered levels. The model should predict stimulation paradigm from the five performance variables (Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD). This treats paradigm as the response and performance as predictors, which is the natural direction for classification. Include Mouse as a random effect via mixed multinomial logistic regression (e.g., using mlogit or brms in R) to account for non-independence. Alternative: random forest or gradient boosting for non-parametric classification, with Mouse held out in cross-validation. Do NOT use ordinary linear regression with paradigm coded as 1-5, as this imposes false ordinality and equal spacing assumptions.",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Normality: Check residuals for Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD using Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests; note Path Efficiency shows extreme right skew (max=29.8 vs mean=0.47) requiring log-transformation or non-parametric alternative",
    "Homogeneity of variance: Use Levene's test; given vastly unequal n (Combined 48846 vs Sham 3505), Welch's ANOVA may be needed",
    "Independence: Violated by repeated measures from same mice; use mixed models or cluster-robust standard errors",
    "Success binary outcome: Check for complete or quasi-complete separation (Sham success rate=0.27 vs Combined=0.78 suggests good separation but verify)",
    "Multicollinearity: Check correlations among performance variables before predictive modeling; AD and Path Efficiency may covary",
    "Sample size adequacy: Combined group dominates (63.7% of data); check for influential observations and ensure minority groups (Sham, Bright Visual Only) have sufficient power"
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Sham shows markedly worse performance: lowest Success (0.273), highest Time-to-Target (4.68s), lowest Path Efficiency (0.308), lowest Average Speed (10.74), and lowest AD (0.236) suggesting straighter but unsuccessful paths",
    "Combined stimulation shows best overall performance: high Success (0.780), fast Time-to-Target (2.56s), high Path Efficiency (0.502), highest Average Speed (12.83), and highest AD (0.399) indicating more exploratory but efficient navigation",
    "Bright Visual Only outperforms Dim Visual Only on all metrics: Success 0.785 vs 0.673, Time-to-Target 2.61s vs 3.14s, Path Efficiency 0.504 vs 0.434, Speed 12.68 vs 11.97, AD 0.387 vs 0.336",
    "ICMS Only and Dim Visual Only show similar intermediate performance, suggesting unimodal stimulation is comparable regardless of modality",
    "ANOVA expected to show highly significant paradigm effects for all variables given large n and substantial mean differences, especially Success and Time-to-Target",
    "Post-hoc tests expected to show Sham significantly different from all active conditions; Combined significantly different from unimodal conditions; Bright vs Dim Visual significant; ICMS vs Dim Visual likely non-significant"
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe imbalance in stimulation paradigm frequencies: Combined (63.7%) vs Sham (4.6%) creates unequal precision and potential variance heterogeneity",
    "Success is binary but treated as continuous in summary; proper analysis requires logistic or beta regression",
    "Path Efficiency shows extreme outliers (max=29.8, 63x the mean) suggesting calculation errors or rare events that may distort parametric analyses",
    "Mouse as random effect is confounded with paradigm if mice were tested in specific paradigms; need to verify crossing structure",
    "No temporal information: learning effects, fatigue, or session effects unaccounted for",
    "AD interpretation as angular dispersion is provided but validation against raw data unavailable",
    "Single replication (Run 1) with temperature=0.25; no assessment of analysis stability across replications or temperatures",
    "Large sample size (n=76655) guarantees statistical significance for even trivial effects; practical significance requires effect size interpretation"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit a mixed-effects multinomial logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as response and the five performance variables as predictors, including random intercepts for Mouse. Use this to compute predicted probabilities and classification accuracy. Additionally, fit separate mixed models for each performance variable with Stim Paradigm as predictor to quantify effect sizes (Cohen's d for continuous variables, odds ratios for Success). Conduct sensitivity analyses: (1) exclude Path Efficiency outliers >3 SD, (2) use non-parametric Kruskal-Wallis for skewed variables, and (3) verify that results hold when randomly subsampling Combined to match Sham n=3505 for balanced inference."
}
